subject: Chemistry
topic: What makes an element a transition element
title: Zinc Is in the d-Block, So Why Is It Not a Transition Metal?
summary: A transition element has an incompletely filled d subshell in its atom or in a common ion. Iron (3d⁶) passes; copper (3d¹⁰ atom) passes through Cu²⁺ (3d⁹); zinc stays 3d¹⁰ even as Zn²⁺, so Zn, Cd and Hg are d-block but not transition metals.

notes.title: 02 – What Makes an Element a Transition Element

keyPoints: A **transition element** has an **incompletely filled d subshell** in its atom **or** in any common ion.
**Cu**: 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ in the atom, but **Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹** → transition metal.
**Zn, Cd, Hg**: d¹⁰ in the atom and in their ions → d-block, but **not transition metals**.

blocks.p: When a d-block atom forms an ion, the **4s electrons leave first**, then 3d electrons.
Zinc, cadmium and mercury keep a full (n−1)d¹⁰ subshell in the atom and in their common ions, so they are not regarded as transition metals, though they belong to the d-block.
